the time-dependent changes in the cross-links and their immediate precursors of collagen in the culture system of osteogenic cells were consistent with those observed in the development of bone collagen.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the early stage of bone collagen cross-link formation in vitro was essentially similar to that in vivo, and that the ratio of dehydro-HL NL to dehydro-DHL NL increased with time in the culture, suggesting that the cross-linking process of bone collagen is not a static one but is dynamic in nature.
the formation of bone collagen cross-link is not a simple process, but is a complex one that is dependent on the time of development of the tissue and the stage of the tissue development.
the early stage of crosslink formation in collagen is characterized by the time lag in the precursor-product transition, and by the time-dependent change of their ratio.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collagen cross-links are not formed immediately after their precursors are formed, and that a minimum amount of collagen is required for the formation of cross-links.

the time lag of a week between the maximum formation of the precursors and the maximum formation of cross-links in our cell culture model may be the minimum essential time needed for the accumulation of collagen to the level necessary for the precursor-product conversion.

the time-dependent development of bone collagen cross-links and precursors in the osteoblast culture system is a good model for the study of the early stage of collagen cross-link formation in vivo, and that the culture system is useful to study the relationship between collagen cross-links and mineralization in bone.
